newsitem.title: FRANCE: Patten says will ignore China-backed legislature.
newsitem.headline: Patten says will ignore China-backed legislature.

text.p: Chris Patten, outgoing British governor of Hong Kong, told a French newspaper that he would ignore a Beijing-endorsed interim legislature due to be chosen on Saturday in the colony.
"...this echo chamber has no place in the political or administrative life of Hong Hong," Patten said in an interview due to be published in the the daily Liberation on Tuesday.
"We will have nothing to do with it in any form because it is reprehensible and unjustified," Patten said.

The interim body is to replace the current chamber when Britain returns Hong Kong to China next July 1. Its formation is favoured by post-handover leader-elect Tung Chee-hwa but opposed by Patten and local democrats.
The interim legislature, to be picked by a China-supervised college of Hong Kong luminaries, will supplant the Legislative Council elected in 1995 under Patten-directed political reforms.

"A quarter of those who are lining up for jobs in this institution were beaten in regular elections. All that is very sad for Hong Kong and it will be a blot on the first months of (Chinese rule)," he said.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule after more than 150 years of British rule.

Patten said the task of the new chamber was clearly to "reduce the number of democrats in the legislature. If that really is the aim, then it raises inevitable questions about China's goals in other domains".
